description: The native window title bar is removed on Windows and Linux and the app content extends to the top edge of the window
steps: Launch the app on Windows
Verify there is no native title bar with the window title and system buttons
Verify the sidebar and main area background reach the top edge of the window
Repeat on Linux

description: Custom minimize, maximize and close buttons with Segoe-style vector icons are shown in the top-right corner over the content
steps: Launch the app
Look at the top-right corner of the window
Verify minimize, maximize and close buttons are shown in that order, overlaying the content
Verify their icons are vector icons from Assets/Icons that look like the Windows Segoe caption glyphs
Verify the icons are the same on Windows and Linux
Verify no window title or app icon is shown inside the window

description: The grid/list view switch is placed next to the search bar and does not overlap the window buttons
steps: Launch the app with the Library tab open
Verify the grid/list switch sits right next to the search bar
Verify the switch does not overlap the minimize, maximize and close buttons
Resize the window to its minimum width and verify they still do not overlap

description: Clicking the minimize button minimizes the window
steps: Launch the app
Click the minimize button
Verify the window is minimized to the taskbar

description: Clicking the maximize button maximizes the window and switches its icon to restore
steps: Launch the app with the window not maximized
Click the maximize button
Verify the window is maximized
Verify the button icon changes to the restore icon

description: Clicking the restore button on a maximized window restores its previous size and switches the icon back to maximize
steps: Launch the app and note the window size and position
Click the maximize button
Click the restore button
Verify the window returns to the noted size and position
Verify the button icon changes back to the maximize icon

description: Maximizing or restoring the window by other means also updates the maximize/restore icon
steps: Launch the app with the window not maximized
Press Win+Up
Verify the window is maximized and the button shows the restore icon
Press Win+Down
Verify the window is restored and the button shows the maximize icon

description: Clicking the close button closes the app
steps: Launch the app
Click the close button
Verify the window closes and the app process exits

description: Window buttons are highlighted on hover like Windows caption buttons, with a red background for close
steps: Launch the app
Hover over the minimize button and verify a subtle light highlight appears
Hover over the maximize button and verify a subtle light highlight appears
Hover over the close button and verify its background turns red
Move the pointer away and verify the highlights disappear

description: Dragging the top strip of the window moves the window
steps: Launch the app with the window not maximized
Press the mouse on an empty spot of the strip along the top edge of the window
Drag the pointer
Verify the window follows the pointer

description: Pressing on interactive controls inside the top strip does not drag the window
steps: Launch the app with the window not maximized
Press and drag on the search bar and verify the window does not move
Press and drag on the grid/list switch and verify the window does not move
Press and drag on the sidebar tabs and verify the window does not move
Press and drag on the window buttons and verify the window does not move

description: Double-clicking the top strip toggles between maximized and restored
steps: Launch the app with the window not maximized
Double-click an empty spot of the top strip
Verify the window is maximized
Double-click the top strip again
Verify the window is restored

description: Dragging a window edge or corner resizes the window
steps: Launch the app with the window not maximized
Drag the right edge and verify the width changes
Drag the bottom edge and verify the height changes
Drag the bottom-right corner and verify both change
Drag the top edge and verify the height changes

description: Dragging the window by the top strip to the left or right screen edge snaps it to that half of the screen
steps: Launch the app on Windows with the window not maximized
Drag the window by the top strip to the left screen edge and release
Verify the window occupies the left half of the screen
Drag it to the right screen edge and release
Verify the window occupies the right half of the screen

description: Dragging a maximized window by the top strip restores it and moves it with the pointer
steps: Launch the app and maximize the window
Press on an empty spot of the top strip and drag down
Verify the window returns to its restored size and follows the pointer
Verify the button shows the maximize icon
